papers.title: Tau-vulnerable medial temporal lobe connectivity drives a functional-to-synaptic cascade in Alzheimer's disease
papers.abstract: Distinct tau-vulnerable and relatively spared subregions exist within the medial temporal lobe (MTL). However, it remains unclear that how functional connectivity (FC), anchored to tau-vulnerable MTL subregions, is related to tau pathology, synaptic dysfunction, and cognitive decline across the Alzheimer's disease (AD) continuum. We here probe into this with resting-state fMRI data from a discovery cohort (ADNI; N = 386; cognitively normal [CN], mild cognitive impairment [MCI], and AD; 144 with 2-year follow-up) and an independent validation cohort at local hospital (N = 100; CN, subjective cognitive decline [SCD], and MCI; 25 receiving high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation [HF-rTMS]). We first separated the MTL into subregions with high and low neurofibrillary tangle (NFT) burden based on histological atlases, and calculated the seed-based whole-brain FC for each subregion. Second, group differences were assessed using ANCOVA, and associations with amyloid-{beta} (A{beta})/tau pathology, synaptic biomarkers, and cognitive performance were examined. Third, serial mediation, cross-lagged, and longitudinal regression analyses were performed to investigate the proposed pathological sequence, with additional evidence from HF-rTMS intervention and autopsy-confirmed Braak staging. Our results showed that, with the development of AD, FC reductions were focused on the high-NFT MTL network, particularly involving the inferior temporal gyrus and precuneus. Baseline tau burden in high-NFT MTL regions was able to predict subsequent FC alterations. Interestingly, FC between the high-NFT MTL and global brain showed region-specific associations with synaptic biomarkers, including negative associations in the cerebellum and positive associations in the precentral gyrus. We also observed a divergent association between the FC and cognition or pathology at different AD stages, shifting from positive in the early stages to negative in advanced AD. Serial mediation analyses supported a pathway linking tau burden to cognitive impairment through altered high-NFT MTL connectivity in the precuneus and occipital regions and subsequent synaptic dysfunction. Cross-lagged and longitudinal analyses further confirmed the proposed temporal sequence. Furthermore, HF-rTMS-related cognitive improvements were partially associated with enhanced synaptic plasticity through changes in precuneus-high-NFT MTL connectivity. Collectively, these findings support a spatiotemporal framework linking the dysfunction of tau-vulnerable MTL network to synaptic impairment and cognitive decline, highlighting high-NFT MTL-based FC as a potential imaging marker tracking AD progression.

papers.title: LLM Embeddings Complement Theory-Driven Language Features and Cognitive Scores for APOE4 and Aβ Prediction
papers.abstract: Spontaneous language offers a scalable, noninvasive approach for identifying biological indicators of preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD). We examined prediction of APOE4 carrier status and cerebral amyloid-beta burden using Cookie Theft picture descriptions from two cohorts of Hebrew- and English-speaking participants (IRAP, N=134; WRAP, N=1,541). Amyloid-beta burden was classified using lowest-quartile, median, and highest-quartile cutoffs, capturing accumulation below conventional amyloid-positivity thresholds. We compared embeddings from pretrained large language models (LLMs) with standard cognitive test scores, reflecting conventional clinical assessment, and theory-driven linguistic features, reflecting traditional language analysis. Embedding-based models achieved the highest F1 scores among constituent models in five of eight tasks involving APOE4 status and global amyloid-beta burden. High prediction disagreement suggested complementary signals across approaches. An any-positive ensemble significantly outperformed every constituent model and a prior-informed random baseline across all eight tasks, and significantly outperformed all constituent models in 21 of 24 regional amyloid-beta tasks. These findings highlight the complementarity of LLM-based, theory-driven, and cognitive measures for predicting AD-related genetic risk and amyloid pathology, and support further investigation of their potential for early screening approaches.

papers.title: Higher platelet counts are associated with migraine risk across three cohorts among more than 21,000 cases
papers.abstract: Objective We assessed potential associations between migraine and complete blood cell count (CBC) data in three large population-based studies. Background Platelets are thought to be involved in migraine pathology through increased activation during an attack. Migraine attacks are often treated with NSAIDs that inhibit platelets, or triptans that target serotonin receptors, with serotonin being most highly expressed in circulation within platelet granules. However, the exact role of platelets in migraine remains unclear. Methods The UK BioBank (UKBB) has CBC data available from baseline blood samples and migraine diagnoses were obtained through self-report and electronic health records. CBC and migraine data from the 1999-2000, 2001-2002, and 2003-2004 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) study were obtained during single exam visits. CBCs were obtained from Framingham Heart Study (FHS) participants. Migraine history was assessed through clinical diagnostic impressions. The UKBB sample (18,919 cases (4,580 incident); 448,339 controls) was the primary discovery cohort for CBCs, with replication meta-analysis done in NHANES (1,887 cases; 7,242 controls) and FHS (395 cases (229 incident); 3,172 controls). Our primary model adjusted for age and sex, with secondary analysis adjusting for additional factors. Sex-stratified, sex-interaction and ancestry-stratified (UKBB only) analyses were also performed. Results Migraine was associated with platelet count (PLT) in the UKBB (OR=1.058, 95% CI [1.043,1.073], p=2.09E-14) and was replicated in the NHANES-FHS meta-analysis (OR=1.074, 95% CI [1.025,1.126], p=0.003). PLT also drove multiple significant signals of PLT-involved CBC ratios. While neutrophil counts and hemoglobin were associated with migraine in UKBB, these did not replicate in FHS-NHANES meta-analysis. Conclusion Higher platelet count is associated with an increased likelihood of migraine. Further studies with longitudinal assessments of CBCs and migraine attacks are needed to further understand the role of platelets in the onset of migraine attacks.

papers.title: Peripheral Blood NADP(H) Redox Metabolism in Alzheimers Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Where Feasible
papers.abstract: Background: The reduced and oxidized forms of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH/NADP) connect cellular reducing power with the glutathione and thioredoxin systems. Peripheral alterations in this network may reflect systemic redox dysregulation in Alzheimer s disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI), but the evidence has not been quantitatively synthesized. Objective: To systematically evaluate peripheral blood NADP(H) redox metabolism and related enzymes in AD and MCI and to perform meta analyses when the available data were sufficiently comparable.

papers.title: Serum brain-derived tau distinguishes acute neurotrauma diagnoses
papers.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) are two common forms of neurotrauma that can present with overlapping clinical features, complicating early diagnosis and management particularly in acute and mixed-trauma settings.1 - 3 Accurate and rapid biological differentiation remains an unmet need.4 We hypothesized that brain-derived tau (BD-tau), an ultrasensitive blood-based biomarker preferentially selective for tau protein originating from the brain, would distinguish TBI from SCI. In a multi-cohort assessment of 342 patients admitted to the neuro-intensive care unit (285 with TBI, 57 with SCI), and 22 controls, baseline serum BD-tau concentrations were markedly elevated in TBI compared with SCI, discriminating between the two populations with high accuracy (area under the curve [AUC]=0.91, 95%CI 0.87-0.96). In paired serum-cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples, serum BD-tau significantly outperformed CSF BD-tau for injury-type discrimination (AUC=0.95, 95%CI 0.89-0.99 vs. 0.80, 95%CI 0.71-0.89). Baseline serum BD-tau also showed superior discrimination of TBI from SCI compared with established blood biomarkers of neurotrauma, including neurofilament light chain, glial fibrillary acidic protein, and ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 (AUC=0.82, 95%CI 0.76-0.88; vs. 0.53, 95%CI 0.43-0.63; 0.67, 95%CI 0.58-0.76; 0.71, 95%CI 0.64-0.79; all DeLong p<0.001). Longitudinally, serum BD-tau remained persistently elevated in TBI, but not SCI, for up to 144 hours post-injury, with distinct temporal trajectories between injury types. Together, these findings indicate that serum BD-tau enables rapid and minimally invasive differentiation of TBI from SCI and may support early clinical decision-making, triage, and enrollment into injury-specific therapeutic trials, highlighting the potential of circulating biomarkers to improve precision diagnostics in acute neurotrauma care.

papers.title: Scalp EEG seizure warning in children under a pre-specified, locked evaluation: confound audit, structured chance levels and a negative result
papers.abstract: Reported performance of scalp electroencephalographic (EEG) seizure prediction is often inflated by lenient evaluation and by the vigilance-state, clock-time and admission-trend structure of monitoring data. We asked how much short-horizon warning survives a pre-specified, locked evaluation. Continuous video-EEG from 21 monitored children (1315 h) formed the development cohort. A statistical-process-control warning method, evaluated under a written protocol, detected 44% of evaluable seizures at 0.48 false alarms per hour, no better than a random predictor (51%, p = 0.86); its statistic moved three times more with vigilance state than with seizure approach. We re-designed it as a state-conditioned, directional scheme on seven global EEG features, froze it with a hash-recorded configuration and time-stamped pre-specification, and estimated its performance by nested leave-one-patient-out cross-validation: 15 of 45 seizures (33%) at 0.47 false alarms per hour, above analytic (21%, p = 0.034) and permutation chance, but a predictor using only clock time, vigilance state and days since admission reproduced most of this, and the signal was confined to the last 30 min. Applied once to two validation cohorts (a second batch from the same unit and the public CHB-MIT database; 101 evaluable seizures), the frozen scheme detected 19 seizures (19%) at 0.60 false alarms per hour against 26% chance (p = 0.96); no secondary endpoint was met, and with the child as the unit of analysis no cohort was above chance. Scalp-EEG warning should be evaluated under pre-specified rules against structured chance levels; the frozen scheme and framework are offered as a reference.

papers.title: Reduced serum carboxymethyllysine is independently associated with Alzheimer's disease
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Advanced glycation end products accumulate in Alzheimer's disease (AD) brain, but the clinical significance of circulating N{varepsilon}-(carboxymethyl)lysine (CML) remains uncertain. We evaluated serum CML as a complementary peripheral biomarker of AD. METHODS: This observational case-control study enrolled 101 patients with clinically diagnosed AD and 91 healthy controls. Serum CML was quantified in 191 participants. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses assessed association and discrimination. A randomly selected subcohort underwent ultrasensitive measurement of amyloid-, tau-, glial-, and neuroaxonal-related biomarkers. RESULTS: Serum CML was lower in AD than controls (median 15.26 versus 23.72 ng/mL; P<0.001). In a complete-case model (n=178), each 1-ng/mL increase was associated with lower odds of AD (adjusted odds ratio 0.727, 95% confidence interval 0.656-0.804). CML alone yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.883. Five-fold cross-validation yielded AUCs of 0.727 for a clinical model and 0.911 after adding CML. In the biomarker subcohort, AD showed lower A{beta}42/A{beta}40 and higher p-tau217; exploratory CML plus p-tau217 discrimination reached an AUC of 0.966 (n=60). DISCUSSION: Reduced serum CML was independently associated with clinically diagnosed AD and may reflect a systemic glycoxidative dimension complementary to canonical biomarkers. Its biological origins and clinical value require external, longitudinal, and biomarker-defined validation.

papers.title: The effect of carotid atherosclerosis and revascularization on cognition and dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Background: Carotid artery atherosclerosis may accelerate cognitive decline and increase dementia risk, but evidence is fragmented and inconsistent, and benefit of revascularization on cognitive outcomes uncertain. Methods: We systematically searched Medline, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Central Register, and Google Scholar for articles published until 11 November 2024, reporting change in cognition or dementia incidence in relation to carotid artery intima-media thickness, plaque, stenosis, and revascularization procedures. We excluded studies that investigated people with dementia, lacked a reference group, or had post-intervention follow-up <30 days. We additionally included new data from the Rotterdam Study, and results from the recent CREST-2 trial. Two independent reviewers extracted study data. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed if data allowed. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, Cochrane Risk of Bias, and ROBINS-I. Results: Of 5592 records identified, 97 studies were eligible, including 43 observational studies (N=100,326) and 54 intervention studies (N=15788, 6 randomized controlled trials). In observational studies, mostly among stroke-free individuals, intima-media thickness was associated with higher dementia risk (hazard ratio per 1-SD increase: 1.07, 95%CI 1.01-1.13; I2=24.8%; 5 studies), as was presence of 50-100% asymptomatic steno-occlusive disease (hazard ratio: 1.48, 95%CI 1.06 -2.07; I2=0.0%, 3 studies). Cognitive outcomes were too heterogeneous for meta-analysis, but 11/20 observational studies reported a significant association between carotid atherosclerosis and global cognition. In non-randomized intervention studies, carotid revascularization improved global cognition (standardized mean difference: 0.73, 95%CI 0.37 -1.09; I2=89.8%), but all studies were at high risk of bias, and heterogeneity was only partially explained by intervention type and study characteristics in meta-regression. Suggested benefit of stenting on cognition among Chinese patients (Standardized effect: 0.86 [0.57-1.16], 197 patients; and 1.09 [0.64-1.53], 90 patients, 2 trials) was not observed in the larger CREST-2 trial (Standardized effect: 0.03 [-0.09 to 0.15] and 0.02 [-0.09 to 0.14]), nor in post-hoc analyses of cognition in the ACAS trial and long-term dementia risk in ACST-1 (HR: 0.98 [0.75-1.28]). Conclusions: Carotid atherosclerosis is associated with increased risk of dementia. Current evidence does not support carotid revascularization for prevention of cognitive decline or dementia.

papers.title: A Multicenter Retrospective Study on the Safety and Efficacy of the Surpass Evolve Flow Diverter System for the Treatment of Intracranial Aneurysms
papers.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of the Surpass Evolve flow diverter system for the treatment of intracranial aneurysms across three medical centers. Methods: A retrospective review was conducted on patients with intracranial aneurysms treated with the Surpass Evolve FDS between March 2023 and May 2024 at three participating centers. Primary outcome measures included the rate of complete aneurysm occlusion (Raymond-Roy class 1) and the incidence of periprocedural major stroke and mortality. Secondary outcomes encompassed follow-up modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores, imaging assessment results, and complication rates. Results: A total of 132 patients (132 aneurysms) were included. The median age was 60.0 years (IQR 52.5?69.0), and 80 patients (66.6%) were female. The complete occlusion rate was 73.3% (88/120). The rate of major stroke was 2.3%, with no procedure-related mortality. At follow-up, 96.9% of patients had an mRS score of 0?2. Multivariate analysis identified non-use of an intraprocedural IIb/IIIa inhibitor and the absence of a branch arising from the aneurysm as independent predictors of complete occlusion. Conclusion: In this real-world, multicenter, retrospective study, the treatment of intracranial aneurysms with the Surpass Evolve FDS was associated with a high rate of complete occlusion and a favorable safety profile. Our findings indicate that complete occlusion was independently predicted by two key factors: periprocedural avoidance of IIb/IIIa inhibitors and a favorable aneurysm morphology without incorporated branches.

papers.title: Feasibility of Vibrotactile P50 Sensory-Gating Assessment Using Portable EEG
papers.abstract: Sensory gating (SG), most commonly quantified using the auditory P50 event-related potential elicited by a paired "double-click" paradigm, is a well-established biomarker of early sensory inhibition that reflects the brains ability to suppress responses to repetitive sensory input. Although auditory SG paradigms have been widely used in both research and clinical settings, they impose an unavoidable auditory load and are generally limited to controlled laboratory environments, reducing their suitability for ecological monitoring and applications in which auditory resources must remain available. This study evaluated the feasibility of a portable vibrotactile sensory-gating system designed to assess inhibitory processing without engaging the auditory or visual modalities. Fifteen healthy adult participants completed both auditory and vibrotactile paired-stimulus conditions using a within-subject experimental design. Vibrotactile stimuli were delivered through transducers positioned on the volar surface of the forearm while electroencephalographic (EEG) activity was recorded using a 32-channel Emotiv EPOC Flex system. Event-related responses were extracted and analyzed using conventional sensory-gating metrics to enable direct comparison between modalities. Vibrotactile stimulation elicited time-locked P50 responses with attenuation of S2 relative to S1. Mean S2/S1 ratios were 0.521 {+/-} 0.041 for the auditory condition and 0.524 {+/-} 0.064 for the vibrotactile condition. The paired difference was 0.0029 (95% CI, -0.0221 to 0.0279), t(14) = 0.249, p = 0.807, dz = 0.064. No statistically significant difference was detected between modalities in this sample. These group-level findings support further evaluation of portable vibrotactile P50 measurement.

papers.title: Donepezil, galantamine and rivastigmine and progression to memantine add-on therapy in Alzheimer's disease: a nationwide cohort study emulating a target trial in the Brazilian Unified Health System
papers.abstract: Background. Donepezil, galantamine and rivastigmine are dispensed free of charge to people with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease in the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS), but their comparative long-term effectiveness in routine care is unknown. Under the national clinical protocol, memantine is added to a cholinesterase inhibitor (ChEI) when the disease reaches the moderate stage, so memantine add-on can serve as a marker of clinical progression. Methods. Nationwide new-user cohort study emulating a target trial in which adults with Alzheimer's disease eligible for a ChEI would be randomly assigned to start donepezil, galantamine or rivastigmine and followed for memantine add-on. We used outpatient medication dispensing authorizations (APAC records of the Outpatient Information System, SIA/SUS) from all 27 federative units, January 2018 to December 2025. We included patients who started a single ChEI between October 2019, after memantine was first recorded nationally, and December 2025, after at least 12 months without anti-dementia dispensing. The outcome was the first memantine dispensing after the index month. Follow-up ended at add-on, recorded death, loss to follow-up (more than 3 observed months without dispensing) or end of data. Deaths were rarely recorded and were treated as censoring. One pseudonymized health card number shared by many patients was excluded, and follow-up ended earlier in the two affected states. We estimated the risk of add-on at 12 to 48 months had all patients started each drug and remained under observation, using stabilized inverse probability of treatment and censoring weights, with 95% confidence intervals (CI) from 200 bootstrap replicates. The analysis assumed no unmeasured confounding or informative censoring given the measured covariates. Results. The cohort included 142 758 new users (donepezil 74 165; galantamine 30 691; rivastigmine 37 902; mean age 77.3 years; 63.0% women), followed for a median of 14 months; 9 812 memantine add-on events occurred. After weighting, all standardized mean differences were below 0.05. The 24-month weighted cumulative incidence of memantine add-on was 9.7% (95% CI 9.4-10.0) with donepezil, 9.0% (8.6-9.4) with galantamine and 5.6% (5.3-5.9) with rivastigmine. Compared with donepezil, the 24-month risk difference was -0.7 percentage points (pp) (-1.1 to -0.3) for galantamine and -4.1 pp (-4.5 to -3.7) for rivastigmine (risk ratio 0.58, 0.55-0.61). Estimates were stable across sensitivity analyses, including a composite outcome that counted unrecorded deaths and dropouts as events (24-month risk difference -4.1 pp, -4.8 to -3.3) and analyses within age groups (risk ratio 0.64 below 75 years). Deaths were almost never recorded in the dispensing data (at most 0.47% of treated patients per year). Conclusions. In routine SUS care, initiation with rivastigmine, mostly as a transdermal patch, was associated with a lower risk of memantine add-on than initiation with donepezil or galantamine. Because disease severity and death are not recorded in the dispensing data, this difference may reflect prescribing patterns or residual confounding by severity rather than slower progression; additional analyses made differential mortality a less likely explanation. It should be confirmed with linked clinical and mortality data.

papers.title: Longitudinal Investigation of Autonomic Symptoms in Biologically Confirmed (SAA+) Parkinson's Disease
papers.abstract: BackgroundAutonomic symptoms are common in Parkinsons disease (PD) and impact quality of life, with unclear relationship to motor and cognitive progression. ObjectiveCharacterize five-year progression of autonomic symptoms in early PD and their association with motor and cognitive outcomes. MethodsWe analyzed data from 874 PD participants and 252 healthy controls (HC) enrolled in Parkinsons Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI). Autonomic symptoms were assessed annually over five years using Scales for Outcomes in Parkinsons disease-Autonomic dysfunction (SCOPA-AUT); affected autonomic domains were defined as domain subscore >1. Clinical measures included MDS-UPDRS and Montreal Cognitive Assessment. Generalized estimating equations evaluated longitudinal changes, adjusting for age, sex, medication, and comorbidities. ResultsAt baseline, 71% of PD participants reported >1 affected autonomic domain, increasing to 85% among 287 PD participants with 5-year follow-up; HCs reporting >1 affected autonomic domain increased from 40% of participants at baseline to 46% among 145 participants with 5-year follow-up. Gastrointestinal and urinary symptoms were most prevalent in PD. Medication use for constipation and urinary dysfunction increased over time in PD. Cardiovascular comorbidities were common and increased in prevalence in both groups. Greater baseline autonomic symptom burden predicted more rapid cognitive, but not motor decline in PD (p=0.002). ConclusionAutonomic symptoms in PD are common at disease onset, near universal after 5 years, and associated with faster cognitive, but not motor, decline, driven by those with severe symptoms. The high prevalence and impact of autonomic symptoms in early PD highlights the importance of early assessment and management of these symptoms.

papers.title: Plasma phosphorylated tau species across neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases: An ONDRI study
papers.abstract: Elevated plasma phosphorylated tau (p-tau) species are proposed as specific biomarkers of Alzheimers disease (AD) pathology but have also been reported in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Their profile across neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases, as well as their discriminatory value when combined with other plasma biomarkers, remain uncertain. We studied 551 participants (ages 40.1 to 87.1 years; 207 women), comprising 506 patients from the Ontario Neurodegenerative Disease Research Initiative (ONDRI) multi-site cohort and 45 amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}) PET-negative cognitively unimpaired controls from the Brain-Eye Amyloid Memory study. Ten diagnostic groups were studied: mild cognitive impairment (MCI), AD, Parkinsons disease subdivided into cognitively unimpaired (CU), MCI, and dementia, frontotemporal dementia (FTD), cerebrovascular disease (CVD) subdivided into cognitively unimpaired (CU) and cognitively impaired (CI), ALS, and the control group. Baseline visit plasma measurements included p-tau217, p-tau181, A{beta}42/40, neurofilament light chain (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). Cross-sectional analyses compared biomarker levels as well as p-tau217-based inference of amyloid positivity status across diagnostic groups. Receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve (ROC-AUC) analyses ascertained the discriminatory capacity of these biomarkers and ratio combinations. Within the ALS group, baseline biomarker measures were also tested for association against baseline clinical features as well as longitudinal measures of neuropsychological change. P-tau217, p-tau181, GFAP, and NfL differed across groups (all P < 0.001). Compared to controls, p-tau217 was elevated in AD and ALS, p-tau181 and GFAP only in AD, and NfL in ALS and FTD. Inferred amyloid-{beta} positivity was more probable in MCI, AD, ALS, and cognitively impaired CVD groups compared to controls (all P < 0.05). The p-tau217 to NfL ratio discriminated ALS from AD with an ROC-AUC of 0.92 (95% CI 0.85-0.97) compared to p-tau217 alone at 0.65 (95% CI 0.52-0.76). No ALS clinical or longitudinal association survived correction for multiple comparisons. Elevated p-tau217 and inferred amyloid-{beta} positivity in ALS provide further evidence that the assay signal is not necessarily specific for AD pathology. However, the use of p-tau217 in combination with NfL provides improved discriminatory power between ALS and AD, supporting the use of plasma biomarker combinations rather than sole reliance on individual plasma biomarkers. Inferred amyloid-{beta} positivity in cognitively impaired CVD may indicate AD and/or cerebral amyloid angiopathy co-pathology. Currently available plasma biomarkers should therefore be used as diagnostic complements and interpreted within clinical context rather than as standalone molecular diagnoses.

papers.title: Computational Modeling of the Acoustic Radiation Force and Viscoelastic Displacement for Transcranial Focused Ultrasound Neuromodulation
papers.abstract: ObjectiveIn transcranial ultrasound neuromodulation (TUS), simulations of the harmonic pressure are often used for treatment planning. However, other mechanisms of energy transfer, such as acoustic radiation force (ARF) and the resulting tissue displacement, are reported less frequently. Furthermore, there is limited guidance on how these mechanisms should be simulated. This study evaluates the numerical convergence and accuracy of different ARF formulations and investigates the simulation of ultrasound-induced tissue displacement in the context of TUS. ApproachTwo simulations steps are used in k-Wave to first simulate the first order acoustic pressure and velocity fields. Subsequently, these fields are used to calculate the ARF using the momentum-flux density tensor, Reynolds stress force, and attenuation force formulations. The ARF is then applied as input for a second viscoelastic simulation to estimate the tissue displacement induced by the ultrasound field. Numerical accuracy and convergence are quantified as functions of the various numerical choices and hyperparameters in the solvers. Main resultsAmong the investigated formulations, the attenuation-force approach proved to be the most robust and the least susceptible to numerical errors across variable medium types and transducer geometries. Within the parameter space relevant to TUS, it is a valid approximation of the momentum flux density tensor formulation. Similar tissue displacement distributions are found across the different ARF formulations. However, the accuracy of the displacement simulation decreases with increasing pulse duration. Finally, recommendations are formulated on the ARF calculation method and on the numerical hyperparameters for ARF and displacement simulations. SignificanceThis study offers guidelines for calculating the ARF and simulating tissue displacement. The proposed framework enables a more comprehensive characterization of ultrasound-mediated energy transfer in TUS.

papers.title: A multi-scale cell-type resolved map of trans-regulatory architecture in the aging human brain
papers.abstract: Mapping genetic effects on distal genes and regulatory programs is essential for understanding how genetic variation influences complex diseases; yet trans-QTL discovery remains limited by weak effect sizes, extensive multiple testing and poor reproducibility. Here, we introduce TransMap, a generalizable computational framework that combines multi-scale trans-QTL mapping with multi-phenotype genetic colocalization to improve the discovery and interpretation of distal regulatory variants. Beyond individual trans-eGenes, TransMap constructs local co-regulatory program phenotypes that account for background expression variation to improve the detection of weak, coordinated distal genetic effects. Across a broad range of simulation settings, TransMap achieved 9.2-36.7% higher trans-QTL discovery power than existing methods while maintaining well-controlled type I error rates. We applied TransMap to bulk and single-nucleus transcriptomic profiles from the aging human brain in the ADSP Functional Genomics Consortium (FunGen-AD), further integrating proteomic, glycoproteomic and metabolomic biomarker measurements (average N=476 donors). Genome-wide fine-mapping of TransMap single-gene and program-level QTL yielded variant annotations with 2.75-2.88x heritability enrichment across 57 complex diseases and traits (average N=307K), with complementary heritability information captured across regulatory scales. Multi-phenotype colocalization identified 49,532 trans-regulatory events supported by shared genetic signals with cis-eQTL or biomarker-QTL, including 1,825 candidate cis-trans-biomarker regulatory configurations. TransMap further revealed an asymmetric cross-cell-type regulatory architecture in which neuronal cis-regulatory signals preferentially associate with coordinated glial trans-regulatory responses, supported by co-culture experiments and spatial transcriptomics. Alzheimers disease (AD) GWAS-prioritized colocalization identified trans-regulatory associations in 115 AD-associated loci, including a KNOP1 cis-eQTL associated in trans with a microglial regulatory program containing MS4A4E, with additional support from statistical mediation analysis. TransMap provides a multi-scale, cell-type-resolved atlas of trans-regulatory variation and a generalizable framework for elucidating the regulatory architecture of complex diseases.

papers.title: Music-Synchronized Gamma Light Stimulation Strengthens Theta-Gamma Coupling in Older Adults with Cognitive Impairment: Results from a Randomized Feasibility Trial
papers.abstract: Noninvasive clinical innovations for restoring gamma activity via sound and light stimulation have the potential to improve memory and cognitive abilities in Alzheimers disease. We assessed whether pairing music with theta- and gamma-band light changes memory-supporting neural dynamics, and whether those changes track cognition. In an ongoing randomized feasibility trial, 38 older adults with cognitive impairment completed eight weeks of an audiovisual intervention. The treatment group (n = 19) listened to self-selected music while viewing light stimulation that consisted of a 39-Hz gamma-band signal modulated by delta- and theta-band musical rhythms. The control group (n = 19) listened to podcasts while viewing synchronized lights without the gamma frequency (delta-band only). Before and after the 8-week intervention, participants completed a face-name association task and the Alzheimers Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive (ADAS-Cog). Individuals in the treatment group showed significant improvements on a face-name association task and the ADAS-Cog. Cluster-based permutation testing showed a larger increase in phase-amplitude coupling between acoustic theta phase and frontal EEG gamma amplitude in the treatment group compared to the control group. Across participants, increases in stimulus-driven theta to EEG-gamma phase-amplitude coupling were associated with improvements in memory. These preliminary results suggest that theta-gamma stimulation delivered through music and lights strengthens cross-frequency coupling, and may correspondingly strengthen associative memory.

papers.title: Cognitive Performance in Prodromal Neuronal α Synuclein Disease
papers.abstract: ImportanceCognitive abnormalities may emerge during prodromal neuronal -synuclein disease (NSD), but their domain specificity and longitudinal course are uncertain. ObjectiveTo characterize baseline cognition and longitudinal change in prodromal NSD compared with healthy controls, NSD-negative genetic carriers, and sporadic Parkinson disease (PD). DesignLongitudinal cohort study using Parkinsons Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI) data, with first visits from July 2010 through April 2026 and up to 4 years of follow-up. SettingMulticenter cohort. ParticipantsHealthy controls (HC; n=244), GBA1 or LRRK2 nonmanifesting carriers without NSD (n=323), prodromal NSD participants recruited through hyposmia or isolated rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder cohorts (n=1640), and sporadic PD (n=824). ExposuresNSD status and clinical cohort. Main Outcomes and MeasuresCognitive summary scores for verbal memory, executive function, processing speed, language, and visuospatial function, and PPMI-defined mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Models adjusted for age, sex, education, and APOE {varepsilon}4 status. ResultsAmong 3031 participants (mean [SD] age, 66.6 [7.0] years; 1322 female [43.6%]), prodromal NSD participants had lower baseline verbal-memory performance than HC (adjusted difference, -0.20 SD; 95% CI, -0.34 to -0.07; adjusted P = .007); NSD-negative genetic carriers did not differ from HC. No other cognitive domain was lower than HC at baseline or longitudinally. In the primary age-adjusted analysis, verbal-memory trajectory differed from HC over 4 years (P = .009), whereas in a smaller age-matched sensitivity subset through year 3, it did not (P = .62); the baseline difference persisted (adjusted difference, -0.28 SD; 95% CI, -0.46 to -0.10; P = .003). Adjusted MCI probability increased from 10.2% to 15.1% in prodromal NSD, compared with 8.4% to 5.0% in HC and 13.4% to 17.7% in PD. The increase was greater than in HC (ratio of annual odds ratios, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.58; adjusted P = .04) but not PD (P = .62). Conclusions and RelevanceProdromal NSD was associated with modestly lower verbal memory and increasing MCI probability relative to HC, without lower performance in other cognitive domains. The baseline verbal-memory difference was robust, whereas the longitudinal trajectory finding was not reproduced in the smaller age-matched sensitivity subset. Key PointsO_ST_ABSQuestionC_ST_ABSWhat cognitive differences characterize prodromal neuronal -synuclein disease, and how do they change over time? FindingsIn this longitudinal cohort study of 3031 participants, prodromal neuronal -synuclein disease was associated with lower verbal memory at baseline than healthy controls, while other cognitive domains were not lower. In the primary age-adjusted analysis, the verbal-memory trajectory differed from healthy controls over 4 years; in a smaller age-matched sensitivity subset through year 3, it did not differ significantly. MeaningCognitive involvement in prodromal neuronal -synuclein disease may be detectable as a modest verbal-memory signal, while longitudinal changes require confirmation.

papers.title: Longitudinal Participation and Cognitive Score Interpretation in the J-TRC Webstudy
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTIONWeb-based registries support remote cognitive assessment for Alzheimers disease research, but participant-driven reassessment raises questions about long-term data yield and interpretation of repeated scores. We evaluated data contribution, selective observation, and retest-dependent estimates of cognitive change in the Japanese Trial-Ready Cohort (J-TRC) Webstudy. METHODSWe analyzed over six years of J-TRC Webstudy data (launched October 2019; registrations through March 31, 2025; assessments through May 31, 2026). We examined data contribution, inactivity, reactivation, score-associated observation, first-exposure contrasts, and sensitivity to retest models and estimators. RESULTSAmong 14,912 registered accounts, 10,863 participants were eligible; 10,645 (98.0%) completed the Cognitive Function Instrument (CFI), 6,419 (59.1%) completed Cogstate, and 5,792 (53.3%) contributed assessments on multiple days. Among those with sufficient opportunity, 19.4% and 14.1% contributed data at or beyond three and five years. After 365 days without assessment, the estimated probability of resuming within two years was 7.2%. Worse prior cognitive scores were associated with lower odds of subsequent assessment (adjusted odds ratios per standard deviation: CFI, 0.952; Cogstate, 0.845). By assessment 12, returnee changes were +0.43 and +1.14 favorable baseline standard deviations (CFI, Cogstate), versus -0.06 and +0.08 in first-exposure contrasts. Marginal CFI time estimates differed under categorical versus flexible retest adjustment (+0.080 versus -0.227 standard deviations/year). DISCUSSIONHigh initial completion was accompanied by limited long-term data contribution. Subsequent assessment was associated with prior scores, and estimated time trends varied by retest model. Reporting assessment histories and testing model sensitivity are important for interpreting repeated online cognitive scores.

papers.title: Optimized phase-targeted auditory stimulation reduces nocturnal spikes in childhood epilepsies
papers.abstract: Interictal epileptiform discharges, so called spikes, are often strongly activated during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep in childhood epilepsies. In children with pronounced spike activation during NREM-sleep, spike burden can be associated with lifelong impaired cognitive functions. This spike activation is also related to alterations in sleep oscillations, specifically slow waves and spindles, which play essential roles in brain maintenance and maturation. These observations suggest that spikes may disrupt sleep-dependent brain processes that are critical for the development of cognitive functions. Phase-targeted auditory stimulation during NREM sleep delivers brief, non-arousing tones at specific phases of ongoing slow waves to modulate sleep oscillations. Recently, our group showed that isolated, less frequent, and thus less expected, tones engage widespread thalamocortical networks, whereas repetitive, regular trains of tones promote habituation and engage more local corticocortical networks. In this study, we use these contrasting stimulation patterns for a targeted modulation of sleep oscillations and examine their interaction with epileptic spikes. In an initial exploratory study (N = 10; age range: 7.3-16.2 years), we used a within-night block design to directly compare responses to the different stimulation patterns. Isolated tones delivered at long interstimulus intervals induced a transient increase in spike rate, whereas down-phase stimulation delivered in trains at short, regular intervals was associated with a significant reduction. We subsequently optimized the train-based paradigm and evaluated stimulation delivered throughout the night in a proof-of-concept study using a counterbalanced, between-night design (N = 5; age range: 4.4-10.7 years). Spike density decreased locally in all patients, providing convergent evidence for the effects observed in the exploratory study. With this mechanistically guided approach, we demonstrate that repetitive down-phase auditory stimulation of slow waves results in a local reduction of epileptic spikes. This framework may provide a rational basis for targeted interventions aimed at reducing spikes and related cognitive impairments.

papers.title: Circulating insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) and short-term functional change in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS): exploratory evidence for systemic trophic-metabolic reserve.
papers.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) exhibit heterogeneous functional decline, potentially influenced by systemic metabolic reserve. We investigate whether circulating insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) is associated with subsequent functional change in ALS. Serum IGF-1 was measured in 37 participants with ALS and 25 healthy controls. Baseline levels were compared between groups, and across disease-duration defined progression categories. Lagged regression assessed whether prior visit IGF-1 level predicted change in Revised ALS Functional Rating Scale (ALSFRS-R) on the next visit, adjusting for inter-visit interval, body mass index, age and sex. Mixed-effects and sensitivity analyses assessed robustness. Baseline IGF-1 did not differ significantly between controls and ALS (mean + SD: 107.3 + 54.3 vs 132.2 + 68.3 ng/mL, p = 0.12), or across progression categories (F(2, 34) = 0.13, p = 0.88). Across 48 intervals from 23 ALS participants, each 1-SD higher IGF-1 from prior visit was associated with 1.40-point less subsequent {Delta}ALSFRS-R decline (95% CI: 0.03 to 2.77, p = 0.045). Generalised estimating equations yielded a similar association ({beta} = 1.50, p = 0.030), whereas small-cluster robust inference showed wider uncertainty (p = 0.084). Repeated IGF-1 showed an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.69, and the lagged association remained positive in all 23 leave-one-participant-out analyses. The IGF-1-by-time interaction was not significant in a random-slope mixed model (p =0.254). Higher circulating IGF-1 may reflect systemic trophic-metabolic reserve associated with short-term functional preservation in ALS, but limited precision precludes definitive prognostic or causal conclusions.

papers.title: Electric and Magnetic Source Imaging in Epilepsy: Anatomical Insights from Realistic Simulations
papers.abstract: Neurosurgery is an effective treatment for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE), but its success depends on the accurate delineation of the epileptogenic focus, approximated noninvasively by electric and magnetic source imaging (ESI/MSI) of high-density electroencephalography (HD-EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG). These modalities have distinct sensitivity profiles; consequently, epileptiform activity detected by one modality may remain undetected by the other. However, the implications of these differences for spike detectability and localization accuracy, and the added value of combined electromagnetic source imaging (EMSI), remain insufficiently characterized under clinically realistic conditions. Here, we characterize HD-EEG and MEG sensitivity profiles and compare ESI, MSI, and EMSI, using realistic simulations with known ground truth. We generated HD-EEG and MEG datasets from cortical, insular, and hippocampal sources across multiple orientations, activated using patient-derived intracranial EEG spike waveforms. Spike sensitivity and localization accuracy were evaluated using dipole scanning, dynamic statistical parametric mapping (dSPM), and linearly constrained minimum variance (LCMV). EEG demonstrated higher spike detection rates and sensitivity for radially cortical sources at gyral crowns and sulcal bottoms (p<0.001), while MEG detected more spikes from tangential cortical sources along sulcal walls (p<0.001). MSI localized tangential sources more accurately than ESI across all methods (p<0.001), while dipole scanning outperformed dSPM and LCMV for cortical and insular sources (p<0.001). EMSI outperformed ESI (p<0.001) but did not improve localization over MSI. These findings suggest that complementary anatomical sensitivities of HD-EEG and MEG may improve epileptogenic source characterization, supporting simultaneous acquisition during the presurgical evaluation of patients with DRE. Key pointsO_LIEEG and MEG exhibit complementary sensitivity profiles, with EEG detecting more spikes from gyral crowns and sulcal bottoms and MEG from sulcal walls. C_LIO_LIMSI provides more focal and precise source localization than ESI, particularly for tangentially oriented sources. C_LIO_LIDipole-based inverse method achieves higher localization accuracy than experimental dSPM and LCMV. C_LI

papers.title: Path to Prevention Platform Trial in Early-Stage Neuronal Alpha-Synuclein Disease: Study Design
papers.abstract: The development of biologically targeted therapeutics (BTTs) that slow Parkinsons disease progression has been hampered by a reliance on testing interventions in clinically defined populations with already advanced pathobiology. Publications on the biological definition and classification of neuronal -synuclein disease (NSD), and the development of the NSD integrated staging system (NSD-ISS), have generated a framework for identifying individuals with NSD prior to the emergence of a clinically defined syndrome. Path to Prevention (P2P) is a phase 2A, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled platform trial designed to assess the safety and efficacy of interventions in an early-stage NSD population. The trial is embedded within the observational Parkinsons Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI), a structure that enables recruitment of participants from the PPMI cohort, leverages existing operational infrastructure, and utilizes data from non-P2P enrolled PPMI participants in the Bayesian statistical modeling. P2P will enroll participants at least 60 years of age with NSD Stage 2B (abnormal -synuclein, dopaminergic dysfunction, and prodromal signs or symptoms without functional impairment) without a clinically defined diagnosis of PD or a related disorder. As a platform trial, P2P will enable the testing of multiple interventions under a Master Protocol at approximately 35 sites across North America and Europe. Interventions are selected from industry-submitted applications based on biological relevance of the targets, and on the adequacy of the safety data appropriate to the target population. Each treatment regimen will have 125 participants on active treatment and at least 125 shared placebo control participants. Participants will remain on treatment for a maximum of 144 weeks or until 96 weeks since the randomization of the last participant. P2P has two primary endpoints, 1) rate of change in mean putamen specific binding ratio from baseline through follow-up and, 2) rate of change in the MDS-UPDRS Part III motor examination from baseline through follow-up or initiation of dopaminergic treatment. A range of secondary and exploratory biomarker-focused endpoints will be assessed. The protocol was developed with input from multiple stakeholders, including people with early-stage NSD, biopharmaceutical industry leaders, and regulatory authorities. P2P is the first trial to test biologically targeted assets in biologically defined prodromal participants utilizing an efficient platform design, which will provide the field with tools to expand therapeutic development, and enable intervention at earlier stages of neurodegeneration. P2P is scheduled to begin enrollment in December 2026 and is committed to data sharing and broad dissemination of learnings from the study.

papers.title: Statistical design of Path to Prevention platform trial in early neuronal alpha-synuclein disease
papers.abstract: The Path to Prevention (P2P) platform trial is a first-in-class, phase 2A, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled learning study. Its design expedites the assessment of investigational therapies for the treatment of early-stage Neuronal -Synuclein Disease (NSD), a biological disease continuum that encompasses and often precedes clinically manifest Parkinsons Disease. P2P is embedded within the Parkinsons Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI), a robust observational longitudinal cohort study on Parkinsons disease progression and a trial-facilitating enrollment framework. A regimen, comprised of an active investigational therapy and a matched placebo control, evaluates a therapeutic candidate within the P2P perpetual platform framework. Multiple regimens can be enrolled, enabling efficient testing of multiple therapeutics. A two-stage randomization scheme determines regimen sample size with 125 participants assigned to a regimens active therapy and a variable number to placebo control. The treated follow up period is a minimum of 96 weeks and a maximum of 144 weeks, with the last randomized participant followed for 96 weeks. As a pioneering interventional trial in early-stage NSD, P2P endpoint selection was critically informed by modeling and analysis of available PPMI data. In P2P, regimens will be evaluated for efficacy using two primary endpoints: 1) a biomarker outcome of Dopamine Transporter Single-Photon Emission Computed Tomography (DAT SPECT) imaging measured by the bilateral putamen Specific Binding Ratio (SBR) and 2) a clinical outcome measured by the Movement Disorder Society-Sponsored Revision of the Unified Parkinsons Disease Rating Scale (MDS-UPDRS) Part III score. Each endpoint will be assessed separately using a longitudinal Bayesian mixed effects model, which compares the active treatment group to the shared placebo control group. The model uses regimen-specific controls at full weight and dynamically discounts controls from other regimens. Additionally, placebo control estimates are supplemented by non-randomized control data from the PPMI cohort. Clinical trial simulations, informed by longitudinal data from 275 P2P-eligible PPMI study participants (Age 60-81, 35% Female, 65% Male), were conducted to evaluate the design. Each regimen is well-powered to detect a 40% slowing in progression for both the clinical and biomarker primary endpoints when comparing active treatment to randomized control data. Supplementing the control estimation with non-randomized, P2P-eligible registry participant data increases power in the explored scenarios up to 4% for each endpoint. The embedded P2P platform trial is a powerful learning study that leverages statistical efficiencies from the platform trial design and established PPMI infrastructure and is poised to advance treatment development in early-stage NSD.

papers.title: Tremor Morphology Toolkit: Waveform Modulation-Based Tremor Phenotyping
papers.abstract: Clinicians typically characterize tremor by its frequency, amplitude, and body region affected. Other aspects also provide critical clues to the type of tremor and its underlying pathophysiology including tremor waveform morphology, consistency across cycles, and variability in amplitude and timing. We introduce the Tremor Morphology Toolkit (TMT), an eight-metric, waveform-derived panel that quantifies these features from upper-limb inertial signals. Using accelerometer and gyroscope recordings from 34 individuals with upper-extremity tremor across four standardized tasks (rest, outstretched, wing-beating, and kinetic), we computed: (i) rSHAPE, cycle-to-cycle shape consistency via pairwise similarity of normalized cycles; (ii) rSINE, sinusoidality, the mean correlation of each cycle with its best-fit sinusoid; (iii) rCVA, the coefficient of variation of cycle amplitude; (iv) rCVD, the coefficient of variation of cycle duration; (v) AWI, amplitude-warping index; (vi) DWI, duration-warping index; (vii) FreqVar, a spectral bandwidth indexing power-weighted frequency spread; and (viii) Amplitude Breathing indices, which quantify slow waxing and waning of tremor amplitude over time from fluctuations in the signal envelope, representing the time-varying amplitude of the tremor waveform. We detail algorithms, parameterizations, and implementation defaults to support reproducible use. TMT is designed to complement conventional frequency-amplitude measures by capturing tremor morphology and modulation in a simple, interpretable framework. It enables objective quantification of features often assessed qualitatively at the bedside, facilitates comparisons across recording conditions, and provides a foundation for validation against clinical labels and disease phenotypes. Future studies can integrate these parameters with electrophysiological measures to investigate mechanisms underlying tremor generation and modulation. HighlightsO_LIIntroducing Tremor Morphology Toolkit (TMT), an eight-metric framework for objective tremor characterization. C_LIO_LICorrelation analysis identified redundant and complementary relationships among tremor-shape features, with sinusoidal waveform characteristics (rSINE), cycle-to-cycle amplitude variability (rCVA), and tremor frequency variability (FreqVar) providing a concise, complementary set for characterizing tremor shape. C_LIO_LIExamination of the alignment between newly defined tremor-shape features and clinician perceptions found that clinicians relied more on envelope-based amplitude dynamics than on individual tremor cycles. C_LI

papers.title: Optimizing Lumipulse plasma pTau217/Aβ42 ratio cutpoints in an Asian cohort with high cerebrovascular disease burden
papers.abstract: The generalizability of FDA-cleared Lumipulse plasma pTau217 / A{beta}42 ratio cutpoints to Asian populations remains uncertain, especially in those with high burden of concomitant cerebrovascular disease (CeVD). We evaluated pTau217, A{beta}42 and their ratio in 205 Singapore-based participants with corresponding amyloid neuroimaging. In-house cutpoints were derived using a three-range strategy targeting 95% sensitivity and specificity. Plasma pTau217/A{beta}42 ratio outperformed pTau217 alone (area under the curve, 0.951 versus 0.925; p=0.004), with comparable performance across CeVD severities. Plasma ratio cutpoints achieved 98% negative predictive value, 88% positive predictive value, and 95% accuracy, classifying 10% as intermediate-risk. Using FDA-cleared cutpoints for our cohort retained 97% sensitivity and negative predictive value but yielded lower specificity (86%), positive predictive value (77%) and accuracy (85%), with 29% classified as intermediate-risk. Our findings support the need for population-specific validation of cutpoints from FDA-cleared blood biomarkers of brain amyloid pathology.

papers.title: Divergent Causes of Death After Ischemic and Hemorrhagic Stroke in the Reperfusion Era: A Contemporary Cohort Study
papers.abstract: BackgroundContemporary data on long-term, cause-specific mortality among stroke survivors are sparse, and much of the existing evidence derives from studies performed before the modern reperfusion era. We sought to characterize long-term cause-specific mortality among stroke survivors to discharge (differentiated by stroke subtype) when compared to in-hospital stroke decedents treated under contemporary standards of care. MethodsUsing a hybrid billing-code/imaging and large language model-assisted chart-review pipeline, we identified adults hospitalized for ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke in the Observational Study of Cardiac Arrest Risk (OSCAR) cohort (Cedars-Sinai Health System, Los Angeles) between 2017 and 2020, followed through June 30, 2025. Cause of death was determined and classified into 10 categories. ResultsAmong 1,344 stroke patients (mean age 74.0 {+/-} 14.9 years; ischemic n=1,036 [77.1%], hemorrhagic n=308 [22.9%]), 203 (15.1%) did not survive the index stroke. Of the 1,141 discharged survivors, 625 (54.8%) died over a median follow-up of 5.2 years. Cerebrovascular causes predominated during index stroke hospitalization (36.0%) but accounted for only 15.5% of post-stroke discharge deaths. Among ischemic stroke survivors, cardiac disease was the leading cause of death (31.6%), with sudden cardiac arrest alone accounting for 10.9% of deaths. Among hemorrhagic stroke survivors, cancer (38.9%) was the leading cause of death. Despite these divergent cause-of-death profiles, overall survival did not differ significantly by subtype (median 5.5 vs 5.8 years; P=0.90). ConclusionsIn this contemporary, reperfusion-era cohort, causes of death shifted from cerebrovascular predominance in the acute phase to heart disease/cardiac arrest after ischemic stroke, and malignancy after hemorrhagic stroke. These findings argue for development of subtype-specific post-stroke surveillance, including structured longitudinal cardiac and sudden-death risk assessment for ischemic stroke survivors.

papers.title: Beyond Haploinsufficiency: Protein Domain and Variant Class Shape Language Outcomes in SYNGAP1-DEE
papers.abstract: BackgroundSYNGAP1-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (SYNGAP1-DEE) is generally considered a haploinsufficiency disorder, yet language development varies considerably between affected individuals. With targeted therapies, including antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), approaching clinical evaluation, understanding genotype-specific differences is increasingly important. We investigated whether expressive language and functional communication are associated with SynGAP protein domains and variant class. MethodsWe analyzed cross-sectional caregiver-reported data linked to genetic reports from the international PATRE SYNGAP1 registry. Of 440 participants, 334 had variants that could be assigned to a protein domain and classified as missense (n=79) or truncating/splicing (n=255). Variants were mapped to seven predefined SynGAP protein regions. The primary outcome was a five-level current expressive language score. Secondary outcomes included acquisition of two-word phrases and CFCS-derived functional communication. Each domain was compared with all other regions within the same variant class using nonparametric tests and age-adjusted ordinal or logistic regression. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction was applied. ResultsMissense variants in the C2 domain (aa248-392; n=28) were associated with markedly poorer expressive language (median score 1 vs. 2; age-adjusted OR 0.16, 95% CI 0.06-0.46; q=0.0025). Only 7.1% had acquired two-word phrases compared with 52.0% of individuals with missense variants outside C2 (OR 0.07; q=0.0023). Functional communication was also significantly impaired (OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.09-0.56; q=0.0052). Conversely, truncating/splicing variants in the PH domain (aa103-247; n=50) were associated with better expressive language (median 3 vs. 2; OR 3.52, 95% CI 1.99-6.24; q<0.001) and more frequent acquisition of two-word phrases (62.0% vs. 31.5%). No corresponding language association was observed for C2 truncating/splicing variants or for variants in the RasGAP domain. ConclusionsLanguage outcomes in SYNGAP1-DEE are associated with both variant class and protein location. The marked impairment associated with C2 missense variants contrasts with the relatively preserved language abilities observed in PH truncating/splicing variants, suggesting that SYNGAP1-related disease cannot be fully explained by a uniform haploinsufficiency model alone. These findings support considering protein domain and variant class in future ASO trials, particularly for patient stratification, endpoint selection, and interpretation of treatment outcomes. Abstract SummaryLanguage outcomes in SYNGAP1-DEE differ according to protein domain and variant class. C2 missense variants are associated with markedly poorer expressive language and functional communication, whereas PH truncating/splicing variants are linked to better language abilities. These findings may inform patient stratification and outcome assessment in upcoming antisense oligonucleotide trials.

papers.title: Cortical Thinning in Adults with Prader-Willi Syndrome: Distribution Across Functional Networks and Associations with BMI and the GH/IGF-1 Axis
papers.abstract: Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) is a rare neurogenetic disorder associated with neuropsychiatric, metabolic, endocrine, and physical abnormalities. Although previous neuroimaging studies have identified regional gray matter alterations, cortical thickness (CT) abnormalities and their distribution across large-scale functional brain networks remain poorly characterized in adults with PWS. We investigated cortical morphology in 23 adults with PWS and 22 age- and sex-matched healthy controls who underwent structural MRI. Cortical reconstruction and surface-based morphometric analyses were performed using FreeSurfer. Between-group differences in CT were assessed using age, sex, and intracranial volume as covariates. Associations between CT and clinical, cognitive, anthropometric, and endocrine measures were examined using Spearman correlations. Significant cortical regions were further mapped onto an a priori functional network atlas. Adults with PWS showed reduced CT in a left-hemispheric cluster involving the inferior precentral gyrus, insula, inferior temporal cortex, and orbitofrontal cortex. This cluster overlapped predominantly with the somatomotor, auditory, cingulo-opercular, language, and frontoparietal networks. Within the PWS group, lower CT was associated with higher body mass index and poorer global functioning. CT was positively associated with IGF-1 levels and was greater in participants with a history of growth hormone therapy during childhood. These findings indicate cortical thinning across regions belonging to multiple functional networks involved in sensorimotor, attentional, language, and executive processes, extending previous volumetric findings. The associations with body mass index, functional measures, and the GH/IGF-1 axis suggest that cortical morphology may reflect an interplay between genetic vulnerability and potentially modifiable metabolic and endocrine factors, raising the possibility of a neuroprotective role for GH/IGF-1 signaling.

papers.title: Memory Self-Awareness Phenotypes are Associated with Alzheimers Disease Biomarker Burden and Clinical Progression in Amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment
papers.abstract: STRUCTURED ABSTRACTO_ST_ABSBackgroundC_ST_ABSAltered memory self-awareness is common in mild cognitive impairment (MCI), but its relationship to Alzheimers disease (AD) pathology and progression remains unclear. MethodsUsing 590 amnestic MCI ADNI participants, memory self-awareness was derived from participant-informant discrepancies on the memory subdomain of the Everyday Cognition questionnaire. Heightened awareness and unawareness subscores were calculated, and k-means clustering identified four phenotypes. Associations with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and positron emission tomography (PET) were examined, and clinical progression was assessed using Cox models. ResultsAware and Unaware groups showed lower CSF amyloid-{beta}, and higher CSF phosphorylated tau and PET amyloid. The Unaware phenotype was associated with increased progression risk (hazard ratio 2.41, 95% CI 1.48-3.92), whereas the Worried Well phenotype showed reduced risk (hazard ratio 0.58, 95% CI 0.34-0.99). ConclusionsMultidimensional assessment of memory self-awareness identifies biologically and prognostically distinct subgroups within MCI and may improve risk stratification in prodromal AD.

papers.title: Suvorexant Inversely Affects Phosphorylated Tau in Human Cerebrospinal Fluid and Plasma
papers.abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) is characterized by amyloid-{beta} plaques and neurofibrillary tangles of tau. Suvorexant, a dual orexin receptor antagonist, was previously shown to acutely reduce the ratio of phosphorylated tau-181 to unphosphorylated tau-181 (pT181/T181) in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). However, its effects on plasma pT181/T181 and broader proteomic networks remain unknown. Here, we conducted a secondary analysis of samples from a randomized, placebo-controlled trial of 25 participants receiving placebo or suvorexant 20 mg. Paired CSF and plasma samples were collected longitudinally via indwelling intrathecal and intravenous catheters. Plasma AD biomarkers were quantified by mass spectrometry, and proteomic profiling was performed using the SomaScan 11K assay on samples from hours 0, 16, and 24. Suvorexant increased pT181/T181 in plasma while decreasing it in CSF between 08:00-16:00. At the pathway level, suvorexant increased the extracellular abundance of proteins associated with translation, RNA binding, cytoskeletal organization and endosomal sorting, centrally at 16 hours and peripherally at 24 hours, and decreased cytokine and receptor-ligand signaling and serine protease activity in plasma at 24 hours. As plasma biomarkers are increasingly used for clinical screening and trial enrollment, factors that influence their levels, including medications, must be identified and their effects on interpretation understood.
